R76 certificates under the OIML Certificate System (basic) — scheme A is the traditional OIML Certificate System, scheme B is MAA (Mutual Acceptance Arrangement). This one is from NWML in 2009, so it's the basic system → scheme "A". The prompt says scheme (A|B). I'll use "A".

- description: "This indicating device is designated the D1050. It is designed to be used as part of a Class III or IIII non-automatic weighing instrument. It operates as single interval, multi-interval or multi-range, and is self-indicating and mains or DC-powered."

Model family: is there >1 model variant? The maximum number of scale intervals varies by configuration (single interval, multi-interval 2 partial ranges, 3 partial ranges; Class III vs IIII). These are configuration variations, not models. Power supply has two options (110-240 VAC 50/60 Hz, or 12 VDC). These are configurations → config_level.

Hmm, do I need model_family? The certificate covers one indicator D1050 with configurations. I think config_level is more appropriate. Maybe no model_family. But the "Maximum number of scale intervals" varies by mode (single vs multi-interval) and class. I'll use config_level with axis like "instrument_mode" and "accuracy_class".

Characteristics type_level:
- power_supply: complex. Split:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min:110, max:240}, unit V — but also alternative 12 VDC. Hmm. Two options: mains 110–240 VAC 50/60 Hz, or 12 VDC. This is config-dependent. I could emit:
    - config_level: attribute power_supply_voltage, axis "power_source" values: [{condition: "AC mains", value: {min:110,max:240}, unit_symbol:"V"}, {condition: "DC", value: 12, unit_symbol:"V"}]
    - power_supply_frequency for AC: {min:50,max:60} Hz
    - power_supply_type: "AC" / "DC"...
  Alternatively simpler: type_level power_supply_voltage_ac {min:110,max:240} V; power_supply_voltage_dc 12 V. Let me use config_level for the voltage since it varies by power configuration.

  Actually the rules say: `110-240V AC 50/60Hz` → SPLIT into three characteristics: power_supply_voltage, power_supply_frequency, power_supply_type. Here there are two supply options. I'll do:
  - config_level: [{attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "AC mains", value: {min:110,max:240}, unit_symbol:"V"}, {condition: "DC", value: 12, unit_symbol:"V"}]}, {attribute: "power_supply_frequency", axis: "power_supply_type", values: [{condition: "AC mains", value: {min:50,max:60}, unit_symbol:"Hz"}]}]

- measuring_range_maximum_voltage: 35 mV

Config-level: axis "load_cell_type": [{condition "analog", value 0.5}, {condition "digital", value 0}] with attribute apportionment_factor_pind? The rule 1 example: apportionment factor pLC → apportionment_factor_plc. So p_ind → apportionment_factor_pind.
- operating_temperature_range: {min:-10, max:40}, unit °C.
- load_cell_cable: 6-wire shielded, max length 2000 m/mm² — hmm "Max length 2000 m/mm²" — likely 2000 m per mm². So max_cable_length: 2000, unit "m/mm²". And cable type: "6-wire shielded" as characteristic load_cell_cable_type value "6-wire shielded".

- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: config-dependent. Emit config_level with axes: interval_mode and accuracy_class. Values:

  - multi-interval/range (2 partial ranges), Class III: 4000
  - multi-interval/range (3 partial ranges), Class III: 3000
  - single and multi-interval/range (2 and 3 partial ranges), Class IIII: 1000

- maximum_tare: "- Max" → value "Max" (i.e., maximum capacity). It's a symbol. Value string "Max"? Rule: formulas/symbols keep as string. "maximum_tare": {value: "Max"}. Hmm "Max" here refers to Max capacity. Keep as "Max".
- maximum_preset_tare: config-level: multi-range single/multi-range → Max; multi-interval → Max₁. Could do config_level attribute maximum_preset_tare axis "interval_mode" values [{condition:"single and multi-range", value:"Max"}, {condition:"multi-interval", value:"Max1"}]. Keep "Max" as string.

Devices: list of peripheral devices. Schema doesn't have devices field explicitly... The characteristics schema has type_level free labels. Could add "devices": but not in schema. Components? These are functions, not sub-assemblies. Maybe skip, or include in description. I could add them under a matrix_tables? No. The schema is layered; rule 8 says don't fabricate fields but the schema is fixed. I could represent devices as components? They're not hardware sub-assemblies named with type designations. I'll append to description? The description already exists. Perhaps add a characteristic type_level "devices" with value string list — but value should be number/string; a list of strings could be value as string. Hmm, value shape is number | {min,max} | string. A long string list is ugly. I'll skip devices or include them in description text. Actually I can add them to description: description includes main features and devices. Let me extend description with main features. I'll keep description concise: the free-text description paragraph plus mention features. I think it's fine to include a fuller description string.

Actually, "Up to 4 load receptors", "Data Storage Device" — those are interfaces/peripheral devices per R76. I'll include them in the description string.
